instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.74(1) requires the Ethics Commission to examine all filed statements and note discrepancies, and §13.685(3) requires the commission to examine each statement filed under §13.68 — establishing a mandatory compliance review by the regulator (not an independent third-party auditor), with subpoena/investigation powers triggered for suspected violations under §13.74(2).

arguments.justification: Section 13.69 prescribes forfeitures up to $5,000 for principals and $1,000 for lobbyists who violate §§13.61-13.68, criminal fines/imprisonment for falsified statements, and Class H felony liability for knowingly filing false registration/reporting statements — covering failures to register, report, and false filings.

content.text:
I'll analyze the statute text for both cells.

**Row 001**: § 13.69 clearly establishes penalties (forfeitures, fines, imprisonment) for various lobbying violations including false statements (§13.69(3), (6m)), unlicensed lobbying (§13.69(4)), and general violations of §§13.61-13.68 (§13.69(1)-(2)).

**Row 002**: § 13.74 requires the commission to examine all statements filed - this is a compliance review by the Ethics Commission, but the commission is the regulator itself, not an "impartial third party" auditor. § 13.685(3) also requires the commission to examine each statement filed under §13.68. This appears to be a compliance review requirement, fitting MODERATE.
